rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and Methods - field experiment on a 0.2 ha cotton field at Akaltyn, Syrdarya province, monitored in 2006-2007 (soil moisture, ECe, groundwater depth, yield) and used to calibrate/validate SWAP; Results, Fig. 3, Table III, Fig. 4 - simulated vs measured soil moisture (RMSE 0.012-0.027) and ECe, simulated yields within 5% of measured. Q2: Scenario analysis, Fig. 9 and Conclusions - the calibrated/validated model simulated five seasonal irrigation regimes (175-400 mm) at a 200 cm water table and found yields rise up to 250 mm with only 3-5% gains above that, so ~3 t/ha can be obtained with 250 mm (vs 2.2-2.5 t/ha measured with 286/175 mm); Table IV and text - WPT/WPET computed for 2006-2007 and the statement that water productivity can be substantially raised by cutting non-beneficial soil evaporation through better irrigation management. Q4: Table IV, Figs 5, 7, 8 - the model quantifies the intermediate variables (soil evaporation ~30% of ETpot, Tact/Tpot, salt storage change, capillary rise qbot, root zone salinity, water table response to irrigation events), with soil moisture and ECe checked against field measurements. Q7: Scenario analysis and Conclusions - the ~3 t/ha with 250 mm holds only if the groundwater table is kept at about 200 cm (drains able to maintain that depth), irrigations must be applied in small amounts to avoid salt inflow, and reaching potential yields requires leaching with freshwater and drainage rehabilitation; findings are stated to apply to the current soil salinity situation. Q8: Discussion/Scenario analysis - SWAP ignores nutrition, pests and diseases (2006 yield reduced by insect attack); crop production is not determined by water table depth alone; measured ECe available for only 2-3 days per season; differences between measured and simulated moisture attributed to soil heterogeneity and observation error; results representative only of present salinity conditions.
rows.notes: Q2 is a qualified yes: the study is a single-field SWAP study whose model is calibrated and validated against measured soil moisture, ECe and yield from the real field, and the scheduling optimisation (irrigation amount x water table depth) is a scenario simulation with that validated model. WP itself is reported only for the two observed seasons (Table IV, 0.52-0.58 kg m-3); the WP gain from optimised scheduling is implied by the yield-vs-irrigation curve (Fig. 9) rather than reported as WP values for the scenarios. Q3 no: one method (model calibrated on field data). Q5/Q6 no: one 0.2 ha field, one crop, one site. Q9 no: only RMSE of calibration and a statement that simulated ECe lies within the standard deviation of measured ECe; no dispersion or uncertainty analysis for the simulated yield/WP results.

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract through references). Study is a single-site field calibration of SWAP followed by scenario simulations of groundwater table depth and seasonal irrigation amount for cotton in Uzbekistan.
